---

Overview

ElevenLabs reads like a quietly editorial print magazine that happens to be a voice-AI product. The base canvas is off-white {colors.canvas} (#f5f5f5) holding warm near-black ink {colors.ink} (#0c0a09). The brand voltage is photographic, not chromatic: soft pastel atmospheric gradient orbs (mint, peach, lavender, sky, rose) drift through the page as the only "color" moments. There is no neon accent, no saturated CTA color, no dark-canvas dev-tools atmosphere.

Type pairs Waldenburg Light (custom serif at weight 300) for display with Inter for body, navigation, captions. The display weight at 300 is the editorial signature — never bold, never heavy.

CTAs are subtle: a near-black ink pill ({component.button-primary}) is the primary, a transparent outline ({component.button-outline}) is the secondary. The brand trusts atmospheric photography and modest type weights to carry brand work.

Key Characteristics:

    Off-white canvas, warm near-black ink. No saturated CTA color.
    Single primary action: ink pill at {rounded.pill}. Atmospheric gradients carry visual brand voltage.
    Display runs Waldenburg Light at weight 300 — editorial magazine voice.
    Body runs Inter at 400 with subtle letter-spacing (+0.15-0.18px).
    Pastel gradient orbs (5 tokens: mint, peach, lavender, sky, rose) used as atmospheric brand decoration only.
    Soft pill geometry ({rounded.pill} for CTAs, {rounded.xl} for cards).
    96px section rhythm.

Colors
Brand & Accent

    Ink Primary ({colors.primary} — #292524): The primary action color — warm near-black pill. Used scarcely.
    Ink Primary Active ({colors.primary-active} — #0c0a09): Press state.

Surface

    Canvas ({colors.canvas} — #f5f5f5): Off-white page floor.
    Canvas Soft ({colors.canvas-soft} — #fafafa): Lighter band for subtle alternating sections.
    Canvas Deep ({colors.canvas-deep} — #0c0a09): Same as ink — used for the rare dark-mode hero (Agents page).
    Surface Card ({colors.surface-card} — #ffffff): Pure white card.
    Surface Strong ({colors.surface-strong} — #f0efed): Badges, voice-icon plates.
    Surface Dark ({colors.surface-dark} — #0c0a09): Dark hero/CTA band canvas.
    Surface Dark Elevated ({colors.surface-dark-elevated} — #1c1917): Cards on dark canvas.

Hairlines

    Hairline ({colors.hairline} — #e7e5e4): Default 1px divider.
    Hairline Soft ({colors.hairline-soft} — #f0efed): Lighter divider.
    Hairline Strong ({colors.hairline-strong} — #d6d3d1): Stronger panel outline.

Text

    Ink ({colors.ink} — #0c0a09): Display, primary text.
    Body ({colors.body} — #4e4e4e): Default running-text.
    Body Strong ({colors.body-strong} — #292524): Same as primary — emphasis.
    Muted ({colors.muted} — #777169): Sub-titles.
    Muted Soft ({colors.muted-soft} — #a8a29e): Disabled text.
    On Primary ({colors.on-primary} — #ffffff): White text on ink pill.
    On Dark ({colors.on-dark} — #ffffff): White text on dark hero.
    On Dark Soft ({colors.on-dark-soft} — #a8a29e): Muted off-white on dark.

Atmospheric Gradient Stops (signature)

    Gradient Mint ({colors.gradient-mint} — #a7e5d3): Mint green orb.
    Gradient Peach ({colors.gradient-peach} — #f4c5a8): Peach orb.
    Gradient Lavender ({colors.gradient-lavender} — #c8b8e0): Lavender orb.
    Gradient Sky ({colors.gradient-sky} — #a8c8e8): Sky-blue orb.
    Gradient Rose ({colors.gradient-rose} — #e8b8c4): Rose orb.

These appear ONLY as soft radial-gradient atmospheric orbs inside {component.gradient-orb-card} and as background atmospheric blooms behind hero copy. Never as button fills, never as text colors.
Semantic

    Success ({colors.semantic-success} — #16a34a): Confirmation.
    Error ({colors.semantic-error} — #dc2626): Validation errors.

Typography
Font Family

Waldenburg Light is the licensed display serif at weight 300. Inter carries body, navigation, captions, and buttons. Fallback: 'Times New Roman', serif for Waldenburg, sans-serif for Inter.
Hierarchy
Token     Size     Weight     Line Height     Letter Spacing     Use
{typography.display-mega}     64px     300     1.05     -1.92px     Homepage hero h1
{typography.display-xl}     48px     300     1.08     -0.96px     Subsidiary heroes
{typography.display-lg}     36px     300     1.17     -0.36px     Section heads
{typography.display-md}     32px     300     1.13     -0.32px     Sub-section heads
{typography.display-sm}     24px     300     1.2     0     Card group titles
{typography.title-md}     20px     500     1.35     0     Component titles — Inter
{typography.title-sm}     18px     500     1.44     0.18px     List labels
{typography.body-md}     16px     400     1.5     0.16px     Default body — Inter
{typography.body-strong}     16px     500     1.5     0.16px     Emphasized body
{typography.body-sm}     15px     400     1.47     0.15px     Footer body
{typography.caption}     14px     400     1.5     0     Photo captions
{typography.caption-uppercase}     12px     600     1.4     0.96px     Section labels, badges
{typography.button}     15px     500     1.0     0     CTA pill
{typography.nav-link}     15px     500     1.4     0     Top-nav menu
Principles

    Display weight stays at 300. Waldenburg Light is the editorial signature. Never bold display copy.
    Subtle letter-spacing on body. Inter at +0.15-0.18px tracking — slightly looser than default Inter for a more editorial feel.
    Negative letter-spacing on display. Waldenburg pulls -0.32px to -1.92px tighter on display sizes.

Note on Font Substitutes

Waldenburg is licensed. Open-source substitute: EB Garamond at weight 300 (slightly more humanist) or GT Sectra (closer to Waldenburg's modernity). Use Inter directly for body — it's the same family ElevenLabs uses.
Layout
Spacing System

    Base unit: 4px.
    Tokens: {spacing.xxs} 4px · {spacing.xs} 8px · {spacing.sm} 12px · {spacing.base} 16px · {spacing.md} 20px · {spacing.lg} 24px · {spacing.xl} 32px · {spacing.xxl} 48px · {spacing.section} 96px.
    Section padding: 96px.

Grid & Container

    Max content width: ~1200px.
    Editorial body: 12-column grid.
    Feature card grids: 2-up at desktop for hero splits, 3-up for benefit grids.
    Footer: 5-column at desktop.

Whitespace Philosophy

Generous editorial pacing — print-magazine feel. 96px between bands; cards inside bands sit close (16-24px gap). The atmospheric gradient orbs occupy generous breathing space without competing with copy.
Elevation & Depth

The system uses hairline + soft drop. Cards float above the off-white canvas via 1px hairlines and a single subtle shadow tier. Atmospheric depth comes from gradient orbs.
Level     Treatment     Use
Flat (canvas)     {colors.canvas} (#f5f5f5)     Body bands, footer
Card     {colors.surface-card} (#ffffff)     Content cards
Hairline border     1px {colors.hairline}     Card outlines
Soft drop     0 4px 16px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.04)     Hovered cards (single shadow tier)
Gradient orb     Radial gradient with one of {colors.gradient-*}     Atmospheric depth — never a card surface
Decorative Depth

    Pastel gradient orbs are the brand's strongest atmospheric pattern. Soft radial blooms in mint, peach, lavender, sky, or rose drift through hero bands and feature sections without containing any content — they are pure atmosphere.

Shapes
Border Radius Scale
Token     Value     Use
{rounded.none}     0px     Reserved
{rounded.xs}     4px     Inline tags
{rounded.sm}     6px     Compact rows
{rounded.md}     8px     Form inputs
{rounded.lg}     12px     Compact cards
{rounded.xl}     16px     Feature cards, pricing tiers
{rounded.xxl}     24px     Gradient orb cards (extra-soft)
{rounded.pill}     9999px     All CTA buttons, badges
{rounded.full}     9999px     Voice icon circles, avatars
Components
Top Navigation

top-nav — Background {colors.canvas}, text {colors.ink}, height 64px. Layout: ElevenLabs wordmark left, primary horizontal menu (Creative / Agents / Video / Pricing / Enterprise / Docs), Sign In + "Try free" primary CTA right.
Buttons

button-primary — Near-black ink pill. Background {colors.primary}, text {colors.on-primary}, type {typography.button} (15px / 500), padding 10px × 20px, height 40px, rounded {rounded.pill}.

button-primary-active — Press state. Background {colors.primary-active}.

button-outline — Transparent pill with 1px ink border. Background transparent, text {colors.ink}, 1px {colors.hairline-strong} border.

button-tertiary-text — Inline ink text link.
Hero & Atmospheric

hero-band — Background {colors.canvas}, full-width display headline in {typography.display-mega} (64px / 300 / -1.92px), subhead in {typography.body-md}, two CTAs, and an atmospheric gradient orb behind the centered headline.

gradient-orb-card — A large card with a soft radial-gradient orb behind centered display copy. Background {colors.canvas-soft}, rounded {rounded.xxl} (24px), padding 32px. Each variant uses one of the five gradient tokens (gradient-mint, gradient-peach, gradient-lavender, gradient-sky, gradient-rose).

audio-waveform-card — A waveform visualization card. Background {colors.surface-card}, rounded {rounded.xl}, padding 24px. Holds a play button + waveform glyph + voice metadata.
Cards

feature-card — 2-up or 3-up grids. Background {colors.surface-card}, text {colors.ink}, rounded {rounded.xl}, padding 24px, 1px hairline border.

product-card-stack — Stacked product preview cards. Background {colors.surface-card}, rounded {rounded.xl}, no padding (children fill the card edge-to-edge).

testimonial-card — Quote card. Background {colors.surface-card}, text {colors.body}, rounded {rounded.xl}, padding 32px.
Voice Library

voice-row — Horizontal row in voice list. Background transparent, 1px hairline divider. Layout: 32px circular voice icon ({component.voice-icon-circular}) left, voice name + accent stack, optional preview button right.

voice-icon-circular — Background {colors.surface-strong}, rounded {rounded.full}, 32px diameter. Holds initials or voice glyph.
Pricing

pricing-tier-card — Background {colors.surface-card}, rounded {rounded.xl}, padding 32px, 1px hairline border.

pricing-tier-featured — Featured tier inverts. Background {colors.surface-dark}, text {colors.on-dark}. Same shape, dark inversion.
Forms & Tags

text-input — Background {colors.surface-card}, text {colors.ink}, rounded {rounded.md} (8px), padding 12px × 16px, height 44px, 1px {colors.hairline-strong} border. On focus, border thickens to 2px ink.

badge-pill — Background {colors.surface-strong}, text {colors.ink}, type {typography.caption-uppercase}, rounded {rounded.pill}, padding 4px × 10px.
CTA / Footer

cta-band — Pre-footer. Background {colors.canvas}, centered display headline in {typography.display-lg}, single ink pill CTA. 96px padding.

footer — Closing footer. Background {colors.canvas}, text {colors.body}. 5-column link list. 64×48px padding.

footer-link — Background transparent, text {colors.body}, type {typography.body-sm}.
Do's and Don'ts
Do

    Reserve {colors.primary} (ink pill) for primary CTAs.
    Use Waldenburg Light at weight 300 for every display headline. Never bold.
    Use Inter at +0.15-0.18px tracking for body — the editorial dialect.
    Use atmospheric gradient orbs (mint/peach/lavender/sky/rose) as decoration only.
    Use the pill shape for every CTA and badge.

Don't

    Don't introduce a saturated brand action color. Ink pill is the only CTA color.
    Don't bold display copy. Display sits at weight 300 — bolding shifts the brand voice from editorial to consumer-marketing.
    Don't use gradient orbs as button fills, text colors, or component backgrounds. They are pure atmosphere.
    Don't use sharp {rounded.none} (0px) on CTAs. Pill geometry is the brand button.
    Don't drop body Inter to weight 300 to match Waldenburg — body stays at 400/500 for legibility.
    Don't extract a CTA color from a third-party widget (cookie consent, OneTrust). The brand's CTA color is what appears on actual product CTAs.

Responsive Behavior
Breakpoints
Name     Width     Key Changes
Mobile     < 640px     Hero h1 64→32px; feature cards 1-up; nav hamburger; gradient orbs shrink.
Tablet     640–1024px     Hero h1 48px; feature cards 2-up.
Desktop     1024–1280px     Full hero h1 64px; feature cards 3-up.
Wide     > 1280px     Content caps at 1200px.
Touch Targets

    Primary pill at 40px height — at WCAG AA, padded for AAA.
    Voice icon circles 32px — padded row creates effective 48px tap zone.

Collapsing Strategy

    Top nav switches to hamburger below 768px.
    Feature grid: 3-up → 2-up → 1-up.
    Gradient orbs reduce diameter at every breakpoint but never disappear.

Iteration Guide

    Focus on a single component at a time.
    CTAs default to {rounded.pill}. Cards use {rounded.xl} (16px).
    Variants live as separate entries.
    Use {token.refs} everywhere — never inline hex.
    Hover state never documented.
    Waldenburg 300 for display, Inter 400/500 for body.
    Gradient orbs scoped to atmospheric decoration.

Known Gaps

    Waldenburg is a licensed typeface; EB Garamond / GT Sectra are documented substitutes.
    Animation timings (orb drift, waveform pulse, hero entrance) out of scope.
    In-product surfaces (voice library editor, agent playground) only partially captured via marketing mockups.
    Form validation states beyond focus not visible on captured surfaces.

OK, here's everything wrong:

1. **Radial glowing orbs** — explicitly banned ("Radial glowing orbs")
2. **Basic pastel colors** — the gradient mint/peach/lavender are pastel
3. **Inter font** — explicitly banned ("Inter, Geist or Space Grotesk")

how is quest connected to the thing

The Quest opens a URL in its built-in browser. The flow:

1. **Interview on a phone/laptop** at `uncle.health` — record, confirm, done
2. The "done" screen builds a link like `uncle.health/xr/?voice=live&name=Ethan&sex=male&head=abc123`
3. **Type that URL into the Quest browser** (or use the QR code / "Open in headset" button)
4. The XR page loads in the Quest's browser, requests WebXR with passthrough, and opens a WebSocket back to `wss://uncle.health/voice`
5. The Quest's mic streams audio over that socket, the server sends back replies (text + audio), and the XR scene plays them through the 3D head

So the Quest just needs Wi-Fi access to `uncle.health` (HTTPS, which it already has via Caddy). No sideloading, no app install — it's all in the browser.

5	## Interview fields (voice -> sim)
6	Gemini fills these from the interview; anything not mentioned stays on its default.
7	```json
8	{ "name": "Ethan", "age": 21, "sex": "male", "province": "ON",
9	  "income_per_year": 30000, "savings": { "tfsa": 2000, "rrsp": 0, "other": 500 },

12	```

14	## Facts sheet (sim -> words, head)
15	Every number the future self may say. Ranges are 10th / 50th / 90th percentile.
16	```json
17	{ "savings_70": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
18	  "income_retired_per_year": { "low": 0, "median": 0, "high": 0 },
19	  "money_lasts_to_90_chance": 0.0,

24	  "sources": [ { "value": "tfsa_limit", "url": "", "fetched_at": "" } ] }
25	```
26	
27	## Placeholders (words -> fill-and-check)
28	The model writes `{savings_70.median}`, never a raw number. Unknown placeholder or raw number = rewrite once, then a template sentence.
29	
30	## Sliders (xr -> sim)
31	`saving_per_month`, `exercise_per_week`, `sleep_hours`, `smoker`. The sim reruns and returns a new facts sheet in under 100 ms.
32	
33	## Voice pipeline
34	The headset connects via WebSocket at `wss://<host>/voice`. One socket per session.
35	
36	**Audio format:** all audio is 16-bit little-endian mono PCM, base64-encoded. Server to headset: 24000 Hz. Headset to server: 16000 Hz. Every message with audio includes a `sampleRate` field.
37	
38	**Session start:** client sends `{ "type": "start", "name": "...", "sex": "male|female", "apparent_age": 70 }`. Server responds with a greeting as normal reply messages.
39	
40	**Messages:**
41	- Client sends: `{ "type": "audio", "data": "<base64 PCM>", "sampleRate": 16000 }` (mic input; server detects end of speech)
42	- Client sends: `{ "type": "text", "question": "..." }` (typed or confirmed question)
43	- Client sends: `{ "type": "age", "apparent_age": 72 }` (slider moved; next sentences use the new age)
44	- Server sends: `{ "type": "transcript", "text": "..." }` (what the user said)
45	- Server sends: `{ "type": "reply", "sentence": "...", "audio": "<base64 PCM>|null", "sampleRate": 24000, "done": false }` (sentence by sentence; `done: true` on last; `audio: null` = text-only fallback)
46	- Server sends: `{ "type": "status", "state": "listening|thinking|speaking" }` (for headset UI)
47	- Server sends: `{ "type": "error", "feature": "...", "message": "..." }` (feature unavailable)
48	- Server sends: `{ "type": "chart", "chart": { "kind": "line|bar|range", "title": "...", "labels": ["..."], "datasets": [{ "label": "...", "data": [0] }] } }` (floating chart panel; sent alongside reply sentences when the topic has visualizable data; XR app renders and makes it grabbable)
49	
50	## Head files (head -> xr)
51	One glTF binary (.glb) per head in `head/builds/<name>/head.glb`. The XR app loads by name. The .glb includes the mesh, texture, and blend shapes for mouth animation. Aged skin variants sit alongside as `head_age<N>.glb` (e.g. `head_age65.glb`, `head_age75.glb`) for slider blending.
52	
53	## Profile endpoint (server -> sim)
54	`GET /api/profile/:name` returns the confirmed interview fields for a user, in the same shape as the interview fields above. The voice session uses this to run `simulate()` on saved profiles; without a saved profile it falls back to `fake-facts.json`.
55	
56	## Saved head library (server)
57	- `/heads.html` lists, searches, uploads and opens saved scans. Existing `head/builds/<id>/head.glb` files are discovered automatically; the head builder and XR loading contract stay the same.
58	- `GET /api/heads` returns `{ heads: [{ id, name, createdAt, bytes, url, xrUrl }], uploadsEnabled }`. `?q=` filters names. `url` downloads the GLB; `xrUrl` opens that scan with live voice and the person's name.

A 24-second video of your head becomes a 3D model, aged in skin, hair and shape, and it talks to you in mixed reality in an aged version of your own voice. 213	### Why we fine-tuned instead of just prompting
214	
215	The guarantee that Uncle never says an invented number comes from the placeholders and our fill-and-check code, which work with any model. The fine-tune is about doing that job faster, more reliably and more in character. We ran the base model, our fine-tune and Gemini (with the same placeholder format and checker) on the same 200 test conversations with random profiles and questions:
216	
217	| Measure | Our fine-tune (Qwen2.5-3B) | Gemini (3.5 Flash Lite) |
218	| --- | --- | --- |
219	| Replies with zero invented numbers (model output, first try) | 171/200 (85.5%) | 199/200 (99.5%) |
220	| Sentences passing check | 93.0% | 99.5% |
221	| Sentences needing rewrite | 7.0% | 0.3% |
222	| Time to write reply | 3,458 ms median | 681 ms median, 808 ms p95 |
223	| After fill-and-check: correct numbers | 100% | 100% |
224	
225	Gemini writes cleaner placeholders on the first try (99.5% vs 85.5%), but after the fill-and-check code both reach 100% correct. The fine-tune's value is staying in character and running on our own Vultr GPU without an external API dependency. The 3B model on a single A16 GPU is slower than Gemini's hosted API (3.5 s vs 0.7 s median), but the voice pipeline's circuit breaker falls back to Gemini when the model is slow, so the user always gets an answer.
226	
227	### Challenges we ran into
228	
229	Reaching the fine-tuned model from the app server. After the model went live on the Vultr GPU, end-to-end voice delay jumped from 1.8 s median to 4.7 s median (10 spoken questions on the live site). Every request was waiting out the model's timeout and then asking Gemini. The cause was the GPU machine's firewall, which blocked port 8000 from the app server; opening that port for the app server's address alone fixed the connection (37 ms from the app server). We also added a circuit breaker so a model failure costs one slow reply, not every reply: after one failure, skip the model for 60 s and use Gemini, with a 2 s model timeout.
230	
231	The model is slower than Gemini on one A16. Timed on the GPU machine itself, a 59-token reply took 2.32 s, about 25 tokens per second, and through the app the reply took 1.8 to 2 s to write against 0.7 s for Gemini. Waiting for the whole reply was the cost, so we stream: the model's words are read sentence by sentence, each sentence is checked and given its real numbers, and the first one is spoken while the rest is still being written. On the live app that cut the time until the first sentence was ready from 1.77 to 1.96 s down to 0.73 to 1.61 s, and the median from end of speech to first audio from 2,777 ms to 2,265 ms (10 questions per run, one laptop, one network). Our target of about 1.2 s is not met.
232	
233	Vultr account limits. Vultr refused to create an A100 (about $1,750 a month) with "maximum monthly fee limit"; the same refusal came from its own command-line tool, because the limit is on the account and counts every running instance together. The message does not state the limit; a teammate reported about $1,000 a month, which fits what we saw. The only upgrade under it was a plan with two A16 cards at $688 a month. A new box we created in Newark never answered on SSH, the same as an earlier box on the other account, and one in Chicago came up in a few minutes.
234	
235	Generating good training data. We iterated through three versions. v1 had 1,240 plain-text examples (85.5% clean on 200 conversations). v2 mixed converted v1 data with fresh JSON-format examples and regressed to 83% because the converted data introduced bad patterns (number words, nested JSON). v3 uses 3,002 fresh Gemini-generated examples with stricter validation (rejecting % after placeholders, nested JSON, sentences over 250 characters) and zero v1 data. Getting the format right so the fine-tune learned to write `{savings_70.median}` instead of a number took iteration on the system prompt, the data generation code, and the sentence-level checker.
236	
237	### Limits and next steps
238	
239	- The fine-tuned model is slower than Gemini (3.5 s vs 0.7 s median in the 200-conversation test, and 1.8 to 2 s through the app) because a 3B model on a single A16 is compute-bound. Streaming and a two-card box shorten the wait; the two-card number (1.29 s for 59 tokens) is a stand-in measurement, and our own model has not yet been timed on that box or through the app. The circuit breaker falls back to Gemini when the model is slow.
240	- A single Vultr GPU handles both model serving and face aging; under load these could compete for memory. A production version would separate them.
241	- The face-aging model's per-head time depends on the number of frames and the GPU model; we have not yet benchmarked it on the Vultr instance.
242

245	## Part 4: MLH Best Use of Gemini API
246	
247	### Uncle for the Gemini track
248	
249	Gemini does two jobs in Uncle. First, it turns a one-minute spoken interview into the simulation's input fields using structured output: the transcript goes in and a JSON object with age, income, savings, habits and province comes out, ready for the Monte Carlo engine. Second, it is the voice of the future self: Gemini 3.5 Flash Lite writes replies using our placeholder format (`{savings_70.median}`, `{life_expectancy.low}`), which our fill-and-check code replaces with real simulation numbers before the user hears them. The fine-tuned model is the primary voice, but Gemini is the fallback and was the only voice for most of the hackathon.

Deployed. Here's what I fixed:

**Problem 1 — Ending session on laptop now ends it in the headset too:**
- Laptop's "End session" button sends a `postMessage` to the spectator iframe

- Also fixed: smart/curly quotes (`\u201c`/`\u201d`) had crept into the `<script>` tag, breaking JS parsing in test and potentially in browsers

**How to test:** Go through the flow on uncle.health, get the pairing code, scan the QR on Quest. The laptop should auto-switch to the spectator view showing the same 3D head, captions, and charts. content.text:
I see the issues:

1. **Retirement age**: The prompt says "retirement_age" but doesn't give much guidance. People say things like "I want to retire around 60" or "maybe at 55" and the model might not catch it. Also the range is [40, 80] which rejects anything below 40.

2. **The prompt is too strict** — "Use ONLY what the person clearly said. If something was not said, return null. Never guess, estimate or assume." This makes Gemini too conservative and misses things people clearly implied.

Let me improve the system prompt to be more lenient and add more examples of how people naturally say things:

input.old_string:
const SYSTEM = `You fill in a form from a short interview with a young Canadian about their money and health habits.
Rules:
- Use ONLY what the person clearly said. If something was not said, return null. Never guess, estimate or assume.
- Never infer sex from the person's name or voice. Only fill "sex" if they say it themselves.
- Convert to the units asked: income_per_year in dollars per YEAR, saving_per_month in dollars per MONTH. Do the arithmetic only when the person gave the numbers (for example "$1200 a year" is 100 a month). If you would have to guess hours or weeks, return null.
- saving_per_month is money the person puts aside each month (or each year, divided by 12). It is NOT a balance: never copy it into tfsa, rrsp, other_savings. Those three are only what they say they ALREADY HAVE saved. If they say they have nothing saved, other_savings is 0.
- "30k" is 30000. Savings amounts are dollars now, split by account (tfsa, rrsp, other_savings) only if they said which; money with no account named goes in other_savings.
- province is the two-letter Canadian code (ON, BC, QC...). exercise_per_week is workouts per week. sleep_hours is hours per night. drinks_per_week is alcoholic drinks per week. smoker is true only if they smoke or vape nicotine now.
- "transcript" is a clean word-for-word transcript of what was said.`;

- "30k" is 30000. Savings amounts are dollars now, split by account (tfsa, rrsp, other_savings) only if they said which; money with no account named goes in other_savings.
- province is the two-letter Canadian code (ON, BC, QC...). exercise_per_week is workouts per week. sleep_hours is hours per night. drinks_per_week is alcoholic drinks per week. smoker is true only if they smoke or vape nicotine now.
- retirement_age: listen for any mention of when they want to stop working, retire, or be done. "I want to retire around 60" = 60. "Maybe 55" = 55. "I want to retire early" = 55. "I never want to retire" = null.
- Be generous with phrasing: "I make like 50 grand" = income_per_year 50000. "I go to the gym three times a week" = exercise_per_week 3. "I get about seven hours of sleep" = sleep_hours 7. "I have a couple drinks on weekends" = drinks_per_week 2 to 4 (pick the middle).
- "transcript" is a clean word-for-word transcript of what was said.`;

whats the proper terminology to talk about monte carlo

In our context:

**Monte Carlo simulation** — that's the correct full term. We simulate 5,000 possible life paths by randomly sampling from real data (historical returns, mortality tables) each year, then report the spread of outcomes.

Key terms to use naturally:

- **"5,000 simulated lives"** or **"5,000 life paths"** — not "iterations" or "trials" (too clinical)
- **"Ranges, not a single guess"** — 10th/50th/90th percentile outcomes
- **"Resampling historical returns"** — we draw from real past years, not a made-up distribution
- **"Population mortality tables from Statistics Canada"** — where the health numbers come from
- **"Median outcome"** — the middle path, not "average" (median is more accurate for skewed distributions and sounds more precise)

For the video, keep it human: *"We run 5,000 simulated versions of your life using real Canadian data — real stock returns, real mortality tables, real CPP and OAS rules — and show you the range of where you could end up, not just one number."*

Don't say "stochastic modeling" or "probability distribution" in the demo — save that for a judge who asks how it works.
